model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) in percentage for six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000) on the x-axis. The y-axis represents ACC (%) and ranges from 40% to 65%. The Base method (black line with circle markers) starts at approximately 39% and increases slightly to about 44% before leveling off. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at around 44%, rises to approximately 50% at 10², and continues to about 57% at 10³. The FT method (blue line with triangle markers) starts at 40%, increases steadily to about 47% at 10², and reaches approximately 48% at 10³. The MEMIT method (purple line with star markers) begins at around 44%, rises to about 51% at 10², and ends at approximately 55% at 10³. The IKE method (red line with triangle markers) starts at about 43%, increases to roughly 46% at 10², and reaches approximately 49% at 10³. The ROME method (green line with square markers) begins at about 51%, rises to approximately 57% at 10², and ends at about 66% at 10³.
